correctness.rationale: Exact support-max formula reduces width to a two-max scalar envelope; minimization occurs at α=m or M. Even q uses central symmetry. For odd q, the support-pair cosine product is at least cos(π/q)>=1/2, forcing both candidate profiles to decrease to the unique support-equalizing angle. The proof accounts for every square and q-gon angular equality case and positive mixing weights, yielding 2q or 4q unoriented normals. The inradius follows from symmetry averaging and a second minimax. Exact q=5 radical and q^-2 asymptotics follow algebraically. The standard-library checker passed 112,000 deterministic random directional inequalities for q=3,...,30 and 28 constructed equality normals; these spot checks are supplementary rather than infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The directly inspected Medgyes paper fixes the volume-maximizing orthogonal square–pentagon structure, but its theorem and proof concern four-volume, not antipodally paired support widths or their minimizing normals. Published mathematical record summaries for exactly the same polygon-join geometry report a nearest-vertex spherical-depth distribution, exterior normal-cone angles and a simplex-volume spectrum; these are different functionals and their reported statements do not imply the width classification. Six targeted semantic queries and multiple external phrase searches located no equivalent formula, converse or dominating parameter theorem. The claim is supported as provisionally original, not certified historically unique.

value.rationale: The family includes the established unique nine-vertex maximal-volume inscribed four-polytope, making minimum width an intrinsic and motivated shape invariant. Rather than a single recalculated value, the theorem classifies the full infinite square–q-gon family and all minimizing directions, discovers exact even/odd doubling and a strict odd-only width-versus-inradius gap, and identifies different limiting thickness coefficients. These precise statements are useful for understanding directional geometry of sphere-inscribed volume optimizers and their polygonal extensions.
